chunks: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn al-Hasan al-Aftas narrated, saying: One day I was with al-Ma'mun, and we were drinking wine until the wine took its effect; he dismissed his companions and kept me behind.

Then he brought out his slave girls, they played instruments and sang. He said to one of them: 'Sing for the one who is settled in Tus.' So she began to recite: 'A drink to those settled in Tus, and to one from the progeny of the Chosen One who is there, who has left us grief. I mean Abu al-Hasan [al-Ma'mun], he has a right upon everyone who is sorrowful there.' Muhammad ibn Abdullah said: He began to weep until he made me weep.

Then he said to me: 'Woe to you, O Muhammad! Do my household and your household compel me to appoint Abu al-Hasan as a standard [of leadership]? By Allah, if he had not been hastened [to death], I would have seated him in my seat [as successor], but he was hastened. May Allah curse Abdullah and Hamza, the two sons of al-Hasan, for they killed him.'
Then he said to me: 'O Muhammad ibn Abdullah, by Allah, I will tell you a strange story, so keep it confidential.' I said: 'What is that, O Commander of the Faithful?'

He said: 'When Zahiriyah became pregnant with Badr, I went to him and said to him: 'May I be your ransom, I have received news that Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far, and Ja'far ibn Muhammad, and Muhammad ibn Ali, and Ali ibn al-Husayn, and al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon them) used to cast divination arrows and did not err. You are the heir of the people and you possess the knowledge that was with them. Zahiriyah is my favorite, and I do not prefer any of my slave girls over her. She has been pregnant more than once, but it always miscarried. Do you have anything in this regard that we can benefit from?'

He said: 'Do not fear its miscarriage, she will be safe and give birth to a healthy boy, the most resembling of people to his mother. Allah has added two things to his creation: an extra finger in his right hand and an extra finger in his right foot.'

I said to myself: 'This is an opportunity, by Allah! If the matter is not as he described, I will remove him.' So I kept waiting for her delivery until labor seized her. I said to the nurse: 'When she gives birth, bring me the child, whether male or female.' I did not feel it but the nurse came to me with the boy as he had described him: extra in hand and foot, like a shining pearl.

So I intended to step down from the matter that day and surrender what was in my hand to him, but my soul did not cooperate with me. However, I handed him the seal ring and said: 'Manage the affair, there will be no opposition from me to you, and you are the one to precede [in leadership]. By Allah, if he had accepted, I would have done so.'

key_terms.أَبُو الْحَسَنِ: Abu al-Hasan, a title often referring to Imam Musa al-Kadhim or Imam Ali al-Rida in this context
key_terms.الْخَاتَمُ: The seal ring, symbol of authority
key_terms.عِتْرَةُ الْمُصْطَفَى: The progeny of the Chosen One (Prophet)

ai.seo_question: What miracle did Imam al-Rida (a.s.) predict regarding the child of al-Ma'mun's favorite concubine?
ai.summary: This narrative from Kitab al-Ghayba highlights the political tension between Caliph al-Ma'mun and Imam al-Rida (a.s.), illustrating the Imam's divine knowledge through the precise prediction of Zahiriyah's son's physical traits. The story underscores the theme of 'Istidraj' or divine testing, where al-Ma'mun, despite witnessing the miracle, remained stubborn in his refusal to fully acknowledge the Imam's authority, a key concept in Shia historiography regarding the Abbasid-Imamate relations.
